name: Czechia
summary: Only descendants are protected, and only for a quarter (adults) or three quarters (minors) of their intestate share. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Czechia has a statutory trust fund; foundations are for public benefit only.
reserved_share: Descendants only (not spouse or parents): minor descendants at least 3/4 of their intestate share, adult descendants at least 1/4 (Civil Code 89/2012, s. 1642 ff). Example on e-Justice: two children of a widowed testator, each statutory share 1/2; minor reserved 3/8, adult 1/8. Paid as a money claim.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Czechia is not a party to the 1985 Hague Trusts Convention (not listed in the HCCH table). Its Civil Code has a statutory 'trust fund' (svěřenský fond, ss. 1448 ff) that is a civil-law adaptation, not a common-law trust. Foundations (nadace, nadační fond) must serve a generally beneficial purpose under the Civil Code, so a family-benefit foundation is not available.
open_questions: The 'public benefit only' rule for nadace and nadační fond and the section numbers (ss. 1448 ff, 1642 ff, 303 ff) are from general knowledge; e-Justice page (updated 2020) does not cover them. Verify against Act 89/2012.
Treatment of foreign trusts (tax and recognition) not sourced.
